id: -385-阿爾塔薛西斯二世的卡杜西亞戰役
theater: 奇利乞亞庇魯斯河下游

battle.name: 阿爾塔薛西斯二世的卡杜西亞戰役
battle.theater: 奇利乞亞庇魯斯河下游
battle.brief: 公元前385年，薩拉米斯王埃瓦戈拉斯趁卡里亞反亂，率希臘雇兵登陸奇利乞亞，於卡杜西亞迎戰阿爾塔薛西斯二世的大軍。密集長矛線列頂住波斯箭幕與騎兵衝擊，塞浦路斯聯軍贏得野戰；國王主力親至後，埃瓦戈拉斯退回島上，終在薩拉米斯圍城中被擊敗。亞述長矛的結陣刺擊法，即此役勝負所在。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 阿爾塔薛西斯二世的卡杜西亞戰役，是公元前385年波斯帝國與塞浦路斯薩拉米斯王國在奇利乞亞南部打的一場野戰。波斯一方屬阿契美尼德帝國中央直轄的西部邊軍體系，由亞美尼亞總督奧龍特斯、薩迪斯總督法爾納巴茲等分行省將領各領一軍，另有身兼陸海指揮權的阿塔弗拉底斯在戰線上協同；兵種包括帝國中央近衛的持矛重步兵、以楮條盾列陣的卡達克步兵、弓手、標槍手、騎兵，以及編制龐大卻難以展開的戰車，糧秣與攻城器械則由安納托利亞與兩河行省沿海一路運往西線。塞浦路斯一方是國王埃瓦戈拉斯一世率領的薩拉米斯王國軍，主力為塞浦路斯本地步兵與弓箭手，外加自希臘本土、小亞細亞與希臘化小城邦雇來的希臘式重裝步兵、投槍兵與輕裝散兵，另有卡里亞起義者組成的輕裝部隊與新月盾投石索手負責兩翼機動，腓尼基諸城提供海運、登陸部隊與後勤支援，埃及法老阿科里斯則在外交與財政上加以援助。整體而言，這是一場帝國行省聯軍對抗小型王國加外來雇兵聯盟的戰爭：正面投入的兵力有限，牽動的卻是地中海東岸整段海岸線。
countriesEn: The Battle of Cardia of Artaxerxes II was a field engagement fought in 385 BC between the Achaemenid Empire and the Kingdom of Salamis in Cyprus, in southern Cilicia. The Persian side belonged to the western frontier establishment of the central imperial government: satraps such as Orontes of Armenia and Pharnabazus, holder of the satrapy of Sardis, each leading a separate column, together with Autophradates, who exercised combined land and naval command in the same theatre. Their order of battle included spearmen of the royal guard, the cardaces infantry who fought from behind wicker shields, archers and javelinmen, cavalry, and a numerically large chariot establishment that could hardly be brought into line; food, arrows and siege material were moved westwards along the coast from the Anatolian and Mesopotamian provinces. The Cypriot side was the army of King Evagoras I of Salamis, built on Cypriot infantry and archers reinforced by Greek-style hoplites, peltasts and light skirmishers hired from the Greek mainland, the Greek cities of Asia Minor and the Hellenistic poleis, together with light troops raised by the Carian rebels, whose crescent shields and slings were meant for work on the flanks. Phoenician cities supplied the shipping, the landing parties and the lines of supply, and the Egyptian pharaoh Achoris gave the revolt diplomatic and financial backing. In strategic terms this was a war between an imperial provincial coalition and a small kingdom joined to a mercenary alliance: modest in the numbers actually engaged on the field, but it drew the whole eastern Mediterranean coast into the quarrel.
people: 事件的核心人物是薩拉米斯王埃瓦戈拉斯一世。相傳其父出自波斯王族，母系則是塞浦路斯人；他長期替帝國作戰，並在公元前401年的庫納克薩之戰站在波斯一方，因而受封為薩拉米斯之王。他希望把這個王位變成實質的獨立君主國，要求取得阿馬索斯與基提翁一帶的控制權並放寬歲貢；國王則要求他放棄奇利乞亞與島上的擴張、照舊納貢，兩邊條件越拉越遠，最終談崩，公元前391年塞浦路斯舉旗反叛。其子尼科克勒斯自幼隨父征戰，在卡杜西亞一役中與父親同在前線統率兵馬，日後亦代表父王與波斯談判，最後以交出薩拉米斯換取家族性命與一份俸祿。波斯方面的關鍵人物是阿爾塔薛西斯二世本人：這位在位於公元前404年至前358年的國王把塞浦路斯視作帝國西線不能容忍的缺口，先後三次派兵遠征，卡杜西亞戰役之後更親率主力進入奇利乞亞。將領層面，以騎兵與海軍著稱的法爾納巴茲是最早被派去對付埃瓦戈拉斯的帝國重臣；亞美尼亞總督奧龍特斯在卡里亞戰線上與起義者周旋多年；阿塔弗拉底斯則在塞浦路斯的陸戰及其後的薩拉米斯海戰中扮演主導角色。卡里亞人一側有本族首領率眾加入埃瓦戈拉斯的聯軍；埃及法老阿科里斯與提爾、西頓等腓尼基城邦的君主在外交上站在反叛者一邊，卻沒有直接派兵進入奇利乞亞。關於此役的具體細節，主要靠多比奧斯《圖書集》與色諾芬的殘篇互相對照，再加上近代學者的整理。
peopleEn: The central figure of the story is Evagoras I, king of Salamis. By tradition his father came from the Persian royal house while his mother was Cypriot; he served the empire for a long time and fought on the Persian side at the battle of Cunaxa in 401 BC, and was rewarded with the kingship of Salamis. He wanted that kingship to become an effective independent monarchy: he demanded control over Amathus and Kition and a lighter tribute, while the king required him to give up his expansion in Cilicia and on the island and to pay his dues as before. The distance between the two sets of terms grew until the negotiation collapsed, and in 391 BC Cyprus rose in revolt. His son Nicocles, raised in the camp, commanded part of the front line at Cardia alongside his father, later negotiated with the Persians on his father's behalf, and in the end bought the survival of his family and a pension by handing over Salamis. The decisive Persian personality was Artaxerxes II himself: a king reigning from 404 to 358 BC who regarded Cyprus as a gap in the western frontier that could not be tolerated. He launched three expeditions against Evagoras and personally led the main army into Cilicia after the battle. Among the commanders, Pharnabazus, famous for his cavalry and his fleet, was the first imperial heavyweight sent against Evagoras; Orontes of Armenia spent years grappling with the insurgents in Caria; and Autophradates took the leading part in the land fighting in Cyprus and afterwards in the naval action off Salamis. On the Carian side their own tribal leaders marched with Evagoras's coalition, while the pharaoh Achoris and the rulers of Tyre and Sidon supported the rebels diplomatically without committing troops to Cilicia. Our knowledge of the engagement itself rests on the fragments of Diodorus Siculus and of Xenophon, collated against each other and reassembled by modern scholarship.
kits: 本卡所錄的亞述長矛，是一柄短柄、長刃、配鐵鏃的刺擊兵器：柄短而刃長，鏃作柳葉形，既可投刺亦可近身再刺，屬亞述步兵的標準裝備。嚴格說來，這種亞述式短柄長鏃長矛並非公元前385年奇利乞亞戰場上的制式武器；它在此戰的位置，是作為「近身結陣、以刺擊定勝負」這一兵種源流與戰法的代表被記錄。卡杜西亞的交戰雙方都配矛：塞浦路斯聯軍中的希臘式重裝步兵用約二公尺的董利亞長矛配圓盾結陣，矛尖出盾縫向前推壓；亞述式短柄長刃矛與之同屬刺擊兵器譜系，優點在出手快、收矛易，於混戰中可連續再刺，適合密集隊形中對壘。波斯方面，人手一矛一弓：楮條盾的卡達克步兵結成方陣，長矛用來頂住對方線列，弓手在後方以密集箭幕支援，輕裝標槍手與投石索手負責騷擾、分割與追擊。卡里亞人用新月形小盾配短彎刀與投石索，善用丘陵與散兵線游鬥。攻城與補給器械方面，波斯方備有攻城塔、撞槌、柴草與填土用的土袋，箭鏃與矛頭由帝國中央兵工供應；塞浦路斯一方靠海運維持糧秣與箭矢補充，並備小型器械以應付薩拉米斯與基提翁方向的城防。埃瓦戈拉斯的聯軍另僱一批熟悉標槍與投石索的希臘輕裝兵，用來在兩翼拉住波斯騎兵的正面衝擊。馬匹與運輸方面，波斯遠征靠御馬與貨運馬隊輸送重裝與糧秣，戰車在崎嶇河谷中作戰效能有限；塞浦路斯與希臘方面以乘馬步兵作偵察、追擊與聯絡。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear recorded on this card is a thrusting weapon with a short shaft, a long blade and an iron head: the haft is short while the blade is long, the head is leaf-shaped, and it can be thrown or stabbed and then stabbed again at close quarters. It was standard kit for Assyrian infantry. Strictly speaking, a short-shafted Assyrian spear with a long head was not the standard weapon on a Cilician battlefield in 385 BC; its place in this battle is as the recorded representative of the lineage of close-order spearmen whose fighting was decided by stabbing. Both sides at Cardia were armed with spears. The Greek-style hoplites in Evagoras's coalition formed up with the doru, a spear about two metres long, and the aspis, pushing their points forward through the shield wall; the Assyrian-pattern short shaft with long blade belongs to the same family of thrusting weapons, and its advantages are a fast thrust and a quick recovery, so that it can be thrust repeatedly inside a melee, which is exactly what a dense formation needs. On the Persian side each man carried a spear and a bow: the cardaces infantry with wicker shields formed squares, using the spear to pin the opposing line, while archers behind them supported with a dense curtain of arrows, and light javelinmen and slingers were tasked with harassment, disruption and pursuit. The Carians carried small crescent-shaped shields with short swords and slings, and were at their best in broken ground and in skirmish order. As for siege and supply equipment, the Persians brought siege towers, battering rams, brushwood and earth-filled bags, with arrowheads and spearheads supplied from the imperial workshops; the Cypriot side kept grain and arrows moving by sea and held small-scale engines against the defences of Salamis and Kition. Evagoras also hired Greek light troops skilled with the javelin and the sling in order to hold the flanks and take the full weight of the Persian cavalry charge. As for horses and transport, the Persian expedition moved heavy infantry and rations on warhorses and pack trains, and chariots were of limited value in the broken river country; the Cypriot and Greek side used mounted infantry for scouting, pursuit and liaison.
tactics: 卡杜西亞位於奇利乞亞南部、庇魯斯河下游的開闊河谷，離海岸不遠，地面平坦而少有遮蔽，這一地形決定了雙方的打法。塞浦路斯聯軍的部署以希臘式重裝步兵的密集線列為核心：長矛前伸、圓盾相接，前列在承受弓箭消耗時以跪姿把盾壓低成牆，後列以矛尖越肩支援，形成可以反覆推拉的接戰面；兩翼配置卡里亞輕裝兵與希臘標槍兵，寬處主動退讓，把波斯騎兵引入狹窄地形再兩面夾擊；埃瓦戈拉斯與尼科克勒斯率預備隊在中央待機，關鍵時刻投入反衝。波斯軍採帝國標準的混合戰術：先用弓手與標槍手在遠距離投射，消耗對方線列的完整，再以卡達克步兵推進、與長矛線咬住，最後由騎兵自兩翼衝擊；龐大的戰車編制在河谷中被地形限制，只能作聲勢與遮蔽之用。進攻次序上，埃瓦戈拉斯選擇主動迎擊而非固守城池，在對方進入平原、尚在行軍狀態時發動反衝，迫其戰線無法同時使用多餘兵力。海路是塞浦路斯一方的生命線：糧秣、援兵與箭矢由基提翁方向海運補充，一旦海運受阻，島上守軍只能靠島內存糧硬撐，這正是埃瓦戈拉斯後來在薩拉米斯圍城中陷入困境的原因。波斯方的補給線則拉得極長，從安納托利亞與兩河行省經陸路運到奇利乞亞海岸，遠征軍越大，糧秣壓力越重。
tacticsEn: Cardia stood in the open valley of the lower Pyramus in southern Cilicia, not far from the coast, on flat ground with little cover, and that terrain settled how both sides fought. The Cypriot coalition built its deployment around a dense line of Greek-style heavy infantry: spears extended and round shields touching, the front rank kneeling and pressing its shields down into a wall when it took arrow fire, the rear rank keeping spear points over the shoulders of the men in front, so that the contact surface could be pushed and pulled again and again. The flanks were given over to Carian light troops and Greek javelinmen, who deliberately gave way in the open in order to draw the Persian cavalry into narrow ground and then closed on it from two sides. Evagoras and Nicocles held the reserve in the centre, ready to throw it into the counter-attack at the decisive moment. The Persian army followed the standard imperial combined arms method: first archers and javelinmen threw from long range to break up the integrity of the opposing line, then the cardaces infantry advanced and locked with the spear line, and finally the cavalry charged from both wings. The very large chariot establishment was hampered by the valley terrain and could serve only to make an impression and to screen movements. In the order of attack, Evagoras chose to meet the enemy in the open rather than to sit behind walls, and launched his counter-attack while the Persian line was still deploying out of column, denying it the use of any reserve. The sea was the lifeline of the Cypriot side: grain, reinforcements and arrows came in by ship from the direction of Kition, and once that shipping was closed the defenders on the island could only live on what was stored there, which is precisely the difficulty Evagoras later faced in the siege of Salamis. The Persian line of supply, by contrast, was stretched to breaking point, carried by land from Anatolia and the Mesopotamian provinces to the Cilician coast, so that the larger the expedition the heavier the burden of rations.
data: 可核對的數字有限，但仍有幾個硬指標。時間上，卡杜西亞之役屬公元前385年，落在阿爾塔薛西斯二世在位的第二十年前後（該王在位公元前404年至前358年），戰事通常記於夏末；其前因是卡里亞人於公元前388至前384年的反亂，其後是自公元前388年前後起、延續至公元前374年、長達十四年的薩拉米斯圍城。空間上，埃瓦戈拉斯的基地薩拉米斯與奇利乞亞海岸之間的海路超過三百公里，作為會合點的卡杜西亞正卡在庇魯斯河下游的陸路與海路交會處，該處足以讓數千名步兵展開成完整線列。規模上，塞浦路斯並非只靠一隊守軍的小國，島上當時存在約九個城邦王國，薩拉米斯一方可投入的兵員當在數千至一萬之間；波斯方面遠征軍帳面人數雖多，卻受制於行軍縱隊與糧秣，實際能同時投入戰鬥的兵力遠低於此。傷亡方面，古代文獻未留下可信的雙方傷亡數，任何精確的死亡人數都是後人推算，本篇不採用。海戰的船數在古代記載中只以數百艘的量級出現，具體數字各家解讀不一，故只保留量級。兵器方面，亞述長矛的尺度可由浮雕與同類遺物推測，全長約在二公尺上下，屬考古推測的範圍值而非某一役的實測值，短柄配柳葉形鐵鏃，與希臘重裝步兵使用的董利亞長矛在刺擊用途上相當接近，便於在同樣結陣密度下互相對刺。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are limited, but a few hard markers remain. On timing: the battle of Cardia belongs to 385 BC, falling in about the twentieth year of the reign of Artaxerxes II, who ruled from 404 to 358 BC, and it is usually placed in late summer. It came after the Carian revolt of 388 to 384 BC and before the siege of Salamis, which began about 388 BC and dragged on for fourteen years until 374 BC. On geography: the sea passage between Evagoras's base at Salamis and the Cilician coast exceeds three hundred kilometres, and Cardia, chosen as the point of rendezvous, sits exactly where the land road and the sea route of the lower Pyramus meet, on ground broad enough to deploy several thousand infantry into a complete line. On scale: Cyprus was not a small state with one garrison; about nine city kingdoms existed on the island, and the Salamis side could put a few thousand to perhaps ten thousand men into the field. The Persian expedition had far larger numbers on paper, but marching columns and rations held down what could actually be fought with at one time. On losses: no ancient source preserves a credible casualty figure for either side, and any exact death toll is a later reconstruction, so none is used here. For the naval action, the number of ships appears in the ancient accounts only as an order of magnitude, several hundred; the precise figures are read differently by different editors, so only the order of magnitude is kept. On the weapon: the scale of the Assyrian spear can be inferred from reliefs and comparable survivals at roughly two metres overall, an archaeological estimate rather than a measurement from any one battle; a short shaft with a leaf-shaped iron head sits close to the doru used by Greek hoplites in thrusting terms, and is therefore suited to mutual stabbing at the same density of formation.
cause: 這場戰爭的起因可以分三層。最深的一層是埃瓦戈拉斯與波斯王室的封地糾紛：相傳他出自波斯王族而母系在塞浦路斯，長期替帝國作戰並在公元前401年的庫納克薩之戰站在波斯一方，因而獲封薩拉米斯王；他希望把王位變成實質的獨立君主國，要求取得阿馬索斯、基提翁一帶的控制權並放寬歲貢，國王則要求他放棄奇利乞亞與島上的擴張勢力、照舊納貢，雙方條件越拉越遠。第二層是阿爾塔薛西斯二世即位後的整體取向：他要收回此前對行省權力的讓步，把塞浦路斯重新收進中央的直接控制，於是以查帳、索地、加派駐軍的方式層層施壓，把埃瓦戈拉斯逼到只剩服從或反叛兩條路。第三層是時機：卡里亞人於公元前388年起事，奇利乞亞沿海亦有騷動，埃瓦戈拉斯判斷這是切斷波斯西部供應線的窗口，於是在公元前385年率軍渡海登陸奇利乞亞，搶在波斯主力反應之前先打一場。戰術上他的目標很清楚：保住海運，用陸軍把波斯人拖在奇利乞亞的平原上，讓島上的盟友看到反叛有望；波斯方面的目標則是先把塞浦路斯這個據點拔掉，再談其他行省的讓步。
causeEn: The origins of this war can be read on three levels. The deepest is the quarrel over fiefs between Evagoras and the Persian royal house. By tradition he was of Persian royal descent on his father's side and Cypriot on his mother's; he had served the empire for a long time and fought on the Persian side at the battle of Cunaxa in 401 BC, and was granted the kingship of Salamis in reward. He wanted that kingship to become an effective independent monarchy, seeking control over Amathus and Kition and a lighter tribute, while the king required him to abandon his expansion in Cilicia and on the island and to pay as before; the gap between the two sets of terms widened steadily. The second level is the general direction of Artaxerxes II after his accession: he meant to take back the concessions made to provincial dynasts and to bring Cyprus once more under direct central control, and he applied pressure in stages through audits, demands for territory and the stationing of additional troops, until Evagoras was left with only two choices, submission or revolt. The third level is opportunity. The Carians rose in 388 BC and the coastal towns of Cilicia were restive, and Evagoras judged that this was the moment to cut the western supply line of the empire; so in 385 BC he crossed the sea with his army and landed in Cilicia, fighting a battle before the main Persian host could react. His operational object was plain: to keep the sea route open, to pin the Persians on the plains of Cilicia with his land army, and to show the island's allies that revolt could succeed. The Persian object was equally plain: to tear the Cypriot foothold out of the empire first, and only then to discuss concessions in the other provinces.
impact: 卡杜西亞的勝負並沒有改變塞浦路斯的歸屬，卻徹底改變了這場戰爭的規模與走向。埃瓦戈拉斯的野戰勝利讓帝國明白，僅靠行省總督拼湊的雜牌軍無法在西線收復失地，阿爾塔薛西斯二世於是把御前主力與海軍同時投入，結果是把一場可以速決的邊境衝突拖成十四年的消耗戰：海軍在公元前394年的薩拉米斯海戰中先拔掉埃瓦戈拉斯的制海權，接著對薩拉米斯長期圍困，最終在公元前374年以攻陷王城收場，埃瓦戈拉斯本人陣亡，薩拉米斯王統就此斷絕，塞浦路斯重入波斯版圖，島上的王位後來落到基提翁的腓尼基王朝手中。對地中海世界而言，塞浦路斯之亂同時把埃及法老、提爾與西頓等腓尼基城邦、以及希臘本土的傭兵市場全部拉進來，東地中海第一次出現跨海權力的長期對抗，這段經歷後來成為色諾芬《居里德》與其他史家筆下大王與行省之爭敘事的重要素材。對波斯帝國自身，這場戰役也暴露了西部的結構性問題：行省總督的邊軍缺乏協同作戰的訓練，御前軍與行省軍之間的指揮鏈冗長，一旦戰線拉長到奇利乞亞以外，補給與命令都會變慢。從兵器史的角度看，卡杜西亞再一次證明近身結陣的長矛線仍然是這類野戰的決定性手段，而這套密集線列加掩體的戰法，正是亞述人幾百年前在兩河流域奠下的傳統。
impactEn: The outcome at Cardia did not change who owned Cyprus, but it transformed the scale and direction of the whole war. Evagoras's field victory taught the empire that patchwork forces raised by provincial satraps could not recover lost ground in the west, and Artaxerxes II accordingly committed the royal main army and the fleet at the same time. The result was that a frontier quarrel that might have been settled quickly turned into a war of attrition lasting fourteen years: the fleet first took away Evagoras's command of the sea in the naval action off Salamis in 394 BC, then Salamis was invested and held under blockade for years, and the matter was finally settled in 374 BC when the royal city fell. Evagoras died in the fighting, the royal line of Salamis was extinguished, Cyprus returned to Persian sovereignty, and the kingship on the island later passed to the Phoenician dynasty of Kition. For the Mediterranean world, the Cypriot revolt pulled into the conflict the Egyptian pharaoh, the Phoenician cities of Tyre and Sidon, and the Greek mercenary market all at once, and the eastern Mediterranean saw its first long contest between powers across the sea; the episode later became material for the narrative of the Great King and his satraps in Xenophon's Cyropaedia and in other historiography. For the Persian empire itself the campaign exposed structural weaknesses in the west: the frontier armies of the satraps were not trained to fight in combination, the chain of command between the royal host and the provincial troops was long, and once the front was stretched beyond Cilicia, both supply and orders slowed down. From the point of view of the history of arms, Cardia once again demonstrated that the close-order spear line remained the decisive instrument of this kind of field battle, and that the doctrine of dense formations covered by shields is the very tradition the Assyrians had established in Mesopotamia centuries earlier.
result: 就卡杜西亞一戰本身而言，結果是塞浦路斯聯軍取勝：埃瓦戈拉斯以希臘式重裝步兵的長矛線列頂住了波斯的前線部隊，逼迫其步兵放棄進攻、騎兵無法展開，最終迫使波斯軍退離陣地；這是埃瓦戈拉斯一生中最漂亮的一場野戰，後世講述塞浦路斯的反抗時，卡杜西亞總是與他的圍城戰役並列。然而戰略上的贏家其實是波斯人。阿爾塔薛西斯二世親率主力進入奇利乞亞後，埃瓦戈拉斯的陸軍失去補給與接應，被迫放棄在奇利乞亞取得的一切退回島上；他在島上再無外陸可依，海上又被波斯與腓尼基聯合艦隊在公元前394年的薩拉米斯海戰中封鎖，薩拉米斯之圍自公元前388年前後打到公元前374年，最後在父親陣亡、兒子尼科克勒斯開城投降之後結束。此後塞浦路斯各城重回亞契美尼德帝國的統屬，島上的王位由基提翁王朝接手，埃瓦戈拉斯一系覆亡。對武器史而言，這場戰役留下的教訓是明確的：在沒有地形遮蔽的河谷平原上，能夠保持線列完整、並在對方的箭雨與騎兵衝擊下維持冷靜的長矛步兵，才是最終的勝者；亞述式短柄長刃長矛所代表的近身刺擊傳統，雖然不是當日的制式裝備，其背後的結陣與刺殺原則卻在卡杜西亞的戰線上被再一次驗證。
resultEn: As a battle in its own right, the result at Cardia was a victory for the Cypriot coalition: Evagoras held the Persian front with the long spear line of his Greek-style heavy infantry, forced the Persian infantry to abandon its attack, kept the cavalry from deploying, and eventually pushed the Persian army off the field. It was the finest field victory of Evagoras's career, and in later accounts of the Cypriot revolt Cardia is always set beside his siege warfare. Strategically, however, the winner was the Persian side. Once Artaxerxes II entered Cilicia at the head of the main army, Evagoras's land force lost its supply and its support and was compelled to abandon everything it had won in Cilicia and fall back to the island. There it had no foreign soil left to stand on, and at sea it was sealed off by the combined Persian and Phoenician fleet in the action off Salamis in 394 BC. The siege of Salamis ran from about 388 BC to 374 BC and ended with the king's death and the opening of the gates by his son Nicocles. After that the cities of Cyprus returned to Achaemenid allegiance, the kingship of the island passed to the dynasty of Kition, and the line of Evagoras was extinguished. For the history of arms the lesson is equally clear: on open river-valley ground with no cover, the side that keeps its line intact and stays calm under arrow fall and cavalry charge, the spearmen in close order, is the side that ultimately wins. The close-stabbing tradition represented by the short-shafted Assyrian spear with its long iron head was not the standard weapon of that day, but the principles of formation and stabbing behind it were tested once more on the line at Cardia.
